sentences.text:
Initially, the petitioners have filed the present petition U/s 163A of MV Act, on 28.09.2015,
claiming compensation of Rs. 20,00,000/-, along with interest @ 18% per annum.

As per the said petition, on 04.05.2015, at about 11:00 a.m, the victim Megha died, in a road traffic accident, that took place near Gohana, Village Mahara, Near Railway Pul, Haryana, when she was travelling in Alto Car bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, along with her husband Sonu and minor Son Shorya.
It was alleged that the said Alto Car, met with the accident with an unknown Trolla.

Along with the petition, the petitioners have placed on record copy of FIR no. 101/15, dated 04.05.2015,
U/s 279/337/304 A IPC, PS Barauda, District Sonipat, Haryana.

The said petition was filed by the petitioners, against Bimla W/o Anand Swaroop i.e. LR of driver/owner of Alto Car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192 (hereinafter referred as R1), as well as against Royal Sundaram General Insurance Company Ltd./insurer of Alto Car.

entities.text: Royal Sundaram General Insurance Company Ltd./insurer
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: (hereinafter referred as respondent no. 2/R2).
As per the petition, the driver/owner of the Alto Car, also died in the accident in question.

3. Written statement was filed by R1, wherein R1 admitted that her deceased husband was the driver/owner of the Alto Car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, when it met with the MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 accident on 04.05.2015.
However, she contended that since Alto car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, was duly insured with R2, therefore, R2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.

4. Written statement was filed by R2, wherein R2 raised the defence that the present petition has been filed by the petitioners, in collusion with R1 however, R2 admitted that at the time of accident,
Alto car was duly insured with R2.
5.
On 29.05.2018, on the application of the petitioners, the claim petition was converted into petition U/s 166/140 of MV Act.
It was also directed, vide the said order, that the petitioners would not be entitled for any interest, from the date of filing of previous petition, till filing of new petition.
The petitioners were also directed to file amended petition.

Thereafter, the petitioners filed fresh petition U/s 166 of MV Act, claiming compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/- along with interest @ 18%
per annum, on 29.05.2018.

6. As per the amended petition, the petitioners alleged that accident has taken place, as the driver of the Alto car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, was rash and negligent, in driving his vehicle, as it was driving his vehicle, at a very fast speed and could not applied brakes properly, due to which, it got struck against a tree, resulting in fatal injuries to the deceased Megha.

7. After filing of the amended petition, R1 again filed the MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 Written statement in which, she denied any rashness and negligence, on the part of her deceased husband, in driving the Alto Car, bearing registration No.
HR-12R-7192.
8.
Written statement was also filed by R2, wherein R2 denied any negligence on the part of Anand Swaroop, in driving the Alto Car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192.
R2 further denied its liability to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

2 9. On the basis of material on record, following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor, on 26.11.2018:-
1.

Whether on 04.05.2015, at about 11:00 a.m. Megha died near Gohana Village,
Mahara, Near Railway Pul, Haryana, due to rash and negligent driving of Alto car bearing registration no.
HR12R-7192, which was driven rashly and negligently by Anand Swaroop ? OPP 2.

Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so to what an extent and from which of the respondents?OPP.
3) Relief.

10. In support of their claim petition, the petitioner no. 1 got himself examined as PW1, by way of evidence affidavit Ex. PW1/A, wherein, he deposed on the same lines, which were mentioned by him, in his petition U/s 166 of MV Act.
He further deposed that after the accident, Megha was removed to PGIMS Rohtak, where she was declared brought dead.
He further deposed that the deceased was 23 years old, was hardworking, has passed B.Sc and was studying in B.Ed.

He further deposed that she used to earn Rs. 20,000/- per month, by giving tuitions of MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 Science and Maths to students of 9th and 10th class.
He further deposed that he has spent Rs. 25,000/- on funeral and religious ceremony and that the deceased left behind him and her minor son, as his only legal heirs.

In his evidence,
PW1 has placed reliance on death certificate of the deceased as Ex. PW1/1, Education certificate of the deceased as Ex. PW1/2 (3 pages), his Aadhar Card as Ex. PW1/3 and Aadhar card of petitioner no. 2 as Ex. PW1/4, birth certificate of petitioner no. 2 as Ex. PW1/5.
11.
PW1 was also cross examined by Ld. Counsel for R1 and R2.

During the course of cross examination, questions were put to PW1, in denial to the aspect of rashness and negligence, on the part of Anand Swaroop, in driving the Alto Car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192.

Further, Ld.
Counsel for R2, has also put questions from PW1, as to the earnings of the deceased, to which PW1 deposed that his wife was not doing any job and she was giving tuitions.
He further deposed that he has not placed on record bank statement of the deceased, PW1 denied the suggestion that he was not dependent upon the deceased.
12. R1 also got herself examined as R1W1, by way of affidavit Ex. R1W1/A, in which she deposed that the accident has taken place, with an unknown trolla and the said version is mentioned in the FIR.
She further deposed that if the petitioners are entitled for any claim, then R2 is liable to pay the compensation.

In her evidence, R1W1 has placed reliance upon copy of DL of her deceased husband as Ex. R1W1/1, copy of RC of Alto car bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, as Ex. R1W1/2, copy of MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 death certificate of the deceased/driver as Ex. R1W1/3 and copy of insurance policy as Ex. R1W1/4.

sentences.text: 3 13. R1W1 was cross examined by Ld. Counsels for the petitioners, as well as R2, wherein she reiterated the contents of her examination in chief, that the accident has taken place, with an unknown Trolla.
14. R2 has examined ASI Sunil Kumar as R2W1, who has brought the copy of FIR and order of acceptance of untrace report as Ex. R2W1/1.
He deposed that he has filed the DAR in the form of untrace report, before Sh. Jogender Singh, Ld. SDJM, Gohana.

15. As per the record brought by ASI Sunil Kumar, untrace report was accepted by Ld. JMFC, vide order dated 08.08.2022.
16.
After conclusion of evidence, the petitioners has again filed an application, for converting the petition, from 166 MV Act to 163A of MV Act, which was allowed vide order dated 04.09.2024.
However, vide said order, right of the petitioners to claim interest was curtailed, from the date of filing of the amended petition, till the date of order, i.e. from 29.05.2018 till 04.09.2024.

Thus, the petitioners would not be entitled for any interest, from 28.09.2015 till 04.09.2024.
17.
Final arguments were thereafter addressed by Ld. Counsels for the parties.
MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 18.
I have heard the arguments, perused the record and given my thoughtful consideration, to the arguments addressed by Ld. counsel for petitioners and Ld. counsel for respondent no. 1 and 2.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO. 1.
19.

In the present matter, though, the issue no. 1 was framed as under:-
Whether on 04.05.2015, at about 11:00 a.m. Megha died near Gohana Village,
Mahara, Near Railway Pul, Haryana, due to rash and negligent driving of Alto car bearing registration no. HR12R-7192, which was driven rashly and negligently by Anand Swaroop ? OPP 20.

However, as the petitioners have already converted the petition from 166 MV Act to 163A of MV Act therefore, the petitioners are not required to prove negligence on the part of driver of Alto Car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, as grant of compensation U/s 163-A of M.V Act, is based upon no fault liability.

21. In the present matter, involvement of the Alto Car, bearing registration No.
HR-12R-7192, in the case accident, and factum of deceased Megha travelling in the Alto car, at the time of accident, which was driven by Anand Swaroop/husband of R1,
is evident from criminal case record.

Both R1 and R2, in their respective Written Sonu And Ors vs Bimla And Ors on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64858093/
4 Statement

sentences.text: , have also admitted that the MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 deceased Megha was travelling in Alto Car bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, which met with the accident.
They only contended that the accident has taken place, with an unknown Trolla.

The factum of death of the deceased Megha in a road traffic accident, stands also corroborated by her postmortem report, as per which, the deceased died, due to antemortem injuries,
sustained by her in road traffic accident.

Accordingly, it is hereby held, that Megha had died in a motor vehicular accident, which took place on 04.05.2015, at about 11:00 a.m., near Gohana village Mahara, Near Railway Pul, Haryana, while she was travelling in Alto car, bearing registration No. HR-12R-7192, being driven by Anand Swaroop/husband of R1 and insured with R2.
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
22. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.

23. In the matter titled as " Helen C. Rebello Vs. Maharashtra"
reported at SRTC, 1999 (1) SCC 90, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:-
"xxxxxx MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD:
09.06.2025 The Court and Tribunals have a duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the amount of compensation, which should be just.

entities.text:
Helen C. Rebello Vs. Maharashtra"
reported at SRTC, 1999 (1) SCC 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
What would be "just"
compensation is a vexed question.
There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb.
Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations.

It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances,and attending peculiar or special features, if any." xxxxx"
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 24.
PW1 Sonu has deposed that the deceased was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month and she was 23 years old, at the time of accident.
He further deposed that he and petitioner no. 2 were financially dependent upon the income of the deceased.

He has placed reliance upon the death certificate of deceased as Ex. PW1/1, Education certificate of deceased as Ex. PW1/2 (3 pages), his Aadhar Card as Ex. PW1/3 and Aadhar card of petitioner no. 2 as Ex. PW1/4, birth certificate of petitioner no. 2 as Ex. PW1/5.
25.
During his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for R2, PW1 deposed that he has not filed bank statement of the deceased.
He deposed that the deceased was giving tuitions however, he failed to place on record, any proof of income of the deceased.

sentences.text: In his evidence, PW1 deposed that the deceased was 23 years old.

Perusal of educational qualification documents of the MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD:
09.06.2025 deceased reveals that as per her mark sheet of her secondary school examination, her date of birth was 30.07.1992.

The accident in question has taken place on 04.05.2015, therefore, the age of the deceased is taken as 22 years, 09 months, 05 days, for the purpose of applying the appropriate multiplier, in terms of provision contained in Schedule-II of M.V. Act.
27.
It is now well settled position that in petition U/s 163-A M.V Act, the multiplier has to be applied at the age of deceased.
Section 163-A M.V Act contains a special provision as to payment of compensation, on structured formula basis, as indicated in Second Schedule to the Act.
The Second Schedule contains a Table, prescribing the compensation to be awarded, with reference to the age and income of the deceased.

28. Recently, Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Appeal bearing No. MAC.APP 369/2013 titled as " Sushila Devi & Anr. Vs. Parvesh Kumar & Anr." decided on 25.04.2016, has been pleased to take the aforesaid view while observing in para-3 of the judgment that as per Second Schedule, it is the age of the victim which would control the choice of multiplier.

entities.text: Sushila Devi & Anr. Vs. Parvesh Kumar & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 29. Now, the next question arises as to how many dependents were left behind by the deceased Megha.
PW1 Sonu has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that both the petitioners were dependent upon the income of the deceased.
In other words, there were two dependents i.e. husband and son of the deceased.

It has been deposed by PW1, that at the time of MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 accident, deceased was B.Sc. Pass, was giving tuitions and earning Rs. 20,000/- per month but, no documents have been placed on record by PW1, to prove the same.

Therefore, the income of the petitioners, is taken as notional income as per the second schedule as 40,000/- per annum and after deduction of 1/3rd from the annual income of the deceased, towards her personal and living expenses, the annual loss of dependency would come out to Rs. 26,666.66/-.( Rs. 40,000 x 2/3).
The total loss of dependency would be Rs. 4,53,333.33 (Rs. 26,666.66 /- x 17), the age of the deceased being 22 years, 09 months, 05 days.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.
4,53,333.33/- (rounded off to Rs. 4,53,334/-), is awarded on account of loss of dependency, in favour of petitioners.
NON PECUNIARY LOSS 30.

As per Schedule-II of M.V Act, the maximum amount which can be awarded under non pecuniary heads in petition U/s 163-A of M.V Act, is Rs. 4500/- ( i.e. Rs. 2000/- on account of funeral expense and Rs. 2500/- for loss of estate).
Hence, a sum of Rs. 4500/- is awarded under this head, in favour of petitioners.

The total compensation is assessed as under:-
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 4,53,334/-

PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 31.
Now, the question which arises for determination, is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Respondent no. 2/insurance company has no statutory defence.
The only evidence that was led by R2, was to prove that the accident has taken place, with an unknown trolla.

Thus, it stands proved, that there is no breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy,
by the insured.
Keeping in view the existence of valid insurance policy, respondent no. 2/insurance company, becomes liable to pay the compensation amount, as it is liable to indemnify the insured.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.
ISSUE NO. 3 RELIEF:-

32. In view of my findings on issues no. 1 and 2, I award a compensation of Rs. 4,57,834/- alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum, in favour of petitioners and against respondent no. 2, w.e.f. 05.09.2024 till deposition of award amount, within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal at SBI, Rohini Court Branch,
Delhi, within 30 days from today, under intimation of deposition of the awarded amount to be given by R2, to the petitioners and their advocate, failing which, R2 shall be liable to pay interest @ 9%
per annum from the period of delay beyond 30 days.

33. R2 is also directed to place on record the proof of deposit of the award amount, proof of delivery of notice in respect of deposit of the amount in the above said bank to the claimants and complete details in respect of calculations of interest etc. in the court within 30 days from today.
MACT No. 151/17 FIR No. 101/15.; PS Barauda, Distt Sonipat DOD: 09.06.2025 Issue no. 3 is decided accordingly.
APPORTIONMENT 34.

Statements of petitioners/claimants namely Sonu (on behalf of himself and on behalf of his minor son Shorya), in terms of Clause 26 MCTAP was recorded on 14.07.2023.
35.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the statements of claimants Sonu, it is hereby ordered that out of total compensation amount, both the claimants,
shall be entitled for an amount of Rs. 2,28,917/- each, alongwith proportionate interest.

36. Out of share amount of petitioner namely Smt Sonu, a sum of Rs. 2,28,917/- is directed to be immediately released to him in his Saving Bank Account No. 41960240999 with SBI, Rohini Court Branch, having IFSC Code No. SBIN0010323.
37.
The entire share amount of petitioners no. 2 namely Shorya shall be kept in the form of FDRs till he attain the age of majority.
